transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-07-19
Start: 09:30 UTC (recorded)
Duration: ~1h15m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel, Alex Gomez, Priya Singh, Samir Ahmed, Elena Torres
Location: Zoom - infra sync channel

Summary:
One-line: align on runtime preservation policy (eviction and graceful degradation), define an OOM test matrix to validate p99 SLOs, and assign owners to update runbooks and automation.

Topics:
- Eviction thresholds and prefix/KV cache behavior
- Staged degradation ordering and fallback rules
- OOM simulation plan (staging) and measurable acceptance criteria
- Runbook / automation changes and rollout gating

Action items (quick): Maya to circulate matrix, Ravi to run sims, Alex to note kernel fallback perf, Elena to draft runbook.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya: okay uh let's, let's kick off. thanks everyone for being on time. main goal today is to get to a concrete eviction matrix and an OOM sim plan so we can validate the p99 impact before the q3 onramp.

[00:00:25] Priya: sounds good. I, I just want to call out stakeholder acceptance criteria — product needs < 5% degradation at p95 and p99 within the staged degrade window, otherwise we need an auto-fallback to the cheaper variant.

[00:00:45] Ravi: yeah and just to add, from SRE side our primary concern is graceful eviction ordering, like we don't want random KV cache flushes that spike CPU and cause thundering herd. so the eviction policy needs to be predictable.

[00:01:10] Alex: (unintelligible) — when you say predictable, do you mean slot-based eviction or LRU with weight? because on our side slot-based lets the scheduler keep affinity, but LRU with weights is easier to implement now.

[00:01:30] Samir: uh I think we should try a hybrid — weight-LRU but with hard slots for pinned prefixes. that way we don't evict the hot-kv entries, and the scheduler can still pack.

[00:01:50] Elena: quick nit, our kernel fallback path right now adds about 6-8ms tail at sequence length 1024 on A100 quantized models, which eats into the p99 budget. if we do wholesale evictions that trigger kernel fallback often, we could breach SLO.

[00:02:12] Maya: okay that's important. so we need to capture fallback frequency in the sim. Ravi, can we instrument fallback counts in staging run?

[00:02:25] Ravi: yes, we can add a metric and trace tag, but we need a clear test matrix first — sequence lengths, concurrency, model variant (FP16 vs quant) and cache hit rates. otherwise the data won't be actionable.

[00:02:50] Priya: table suggestion — 4 sequence buckets (128, 512, 1024, 2048), concurrency sweep at 1, 8, 32, and cache hit scenarios at 20%, 50%, 80%. also run with quantized and non-quantized.

[00:03:18] Alex: yeah that works. also include cold-starts vs warmed KV cache. I remember last run where cold prefix caused spikes, the trace said K V cache miss but the transcript thing spelled it as K-V cash in the logs, weird.

[00:03:40] Samir: (laughs) the transcriptions will always be weird. but seriously, we should also stress the scheduler: e.g., force tail-latency by pushing mixed model traffic so the packing heuristics get exercised.

[00:03:58] Elena: and add the 'padded sequence' path — models with padding create hidden overhead. include that.

[00:04:10] Maya: good. next: staged degradation ordering. we need the sequence of actions when memory pressure hits a threshold: 1) soft throttling (reject/queue), 2) prefix eviction, 3) fallback to smaller model variant in same family, 4) region failover if still degraded. is everyone aligned on that ordering?

[00:04:35] Ravi: question — is region failover automatic or a last resort manual trigger? auto-failover risks data residency and cross-region costs.

[00:04:48] Priya: product preference is manual for customers with strict residency; automatic for customers who opted-in for resilience. we should have a per-customer policy flag.

[00:05:05] Alex: technical feasibility: we can mark a per-tenant routing flag. the control plane already supports region routing, but we need safeguards in the control plane to prevent flapping. that's an infra task.

[00:05:25] Samir: and we need to ensure KV cache warming on the target region isn't assumed — otherwise failover will see increased latency and timeouts. maybe we pre-warm some prefixes for critical tenants.

[00:05:45] Maya: okay so per-tenant policy + pre-warm option. Elena, you had concerns about quantization skew and degradation?

[00:05:58] Elena: yeah, sad truth — quantized variants sometime introduce subtle generation differences that can change downstream quality metrics. the optimize team flagged a regression last week. so the policy should prefer smaller FP16 variants if quality drop is unacceptable. we need to add eval triggers into the sim.

[00:06:22] Priya: can we have a short blackbox eval — generate a set of prompts and compare rouge/bertscores or whatever the quality metric is we use — to ensure fallback doesn't break customer expectations?

[00:06:40] Ravi: we can hook in the eval harness during the sim, but note it will add time to each run. maybe sample.

[00:06:55] Maya: alright detail the sim scope: Alex and Ravi will define the infra config and test harness, Samir will script the traffic patterns, Elena will define the eval prompts and acceptance thresholds, Maya and Priya will own stakeholder acceptance.

[00:07:14] Alex: regarding the kernel fallback matrix — I'll produce a doc that lists per-model fallback cost (ms), memory delta, and observed p99 delta. expect initial numbers by Friday.

[00:07:30] Elena: and I'll add the quality delta for quant vs fp16. I'll attach notes to the kernel doc.

[00:07:41] Ravi: for the sim schedule, we should avoid running at peak hours in staging — try low-traffic window Tuesday night. also, we need to simulate background housekeeping tasks that normally run on the nodes — those can push a node over the edge during an otherwise synthetic load.

[00:08:05] Samir: good call. I'll add background tasks to the harness. also, note that the autoscaler sometimes reacts late — we need to decide if the sim includes autoscaler behavior or fixed capacity.

[00:08:22] Maya: decision: sim to run in two modes — fixed-capacity (to measure pure scheduling/eviction behavior) and autoscale-on (to observe interaction with scaling). both sets of results required.

[00:08:40] Priya: can we codify acceptance criteria now? product is asking:
  - p95 degradation < 5%
  - p99 degradation < 10% unless customer opted into aggressive degradation
  - no silent errors or silent generation truncation; any truncation must be logged and counted as failure

[00:09:05] Elena: we should also add "fallback frequency budget": e.g., no more than X fallbacks per 10k requests per minute, else auto-rollback.

[00:09:20] Ravi: ok add that. I'll propose numbers in the matrix.

[00:09:32] Maya: routing policy and control plane: Alex, you mentioned flapping safeguards. what do you need from product?

[00:09:42] Alex: a small policy model: thresholds, cooldown windows, per-tenant opt-in. I can prototype default values but need product sign-off.

[00:09:55] Priya: sign-off will be short once we have the matrix + sim results.

[00:10:05] Maya: great. any other technical deep dives?

[00:10:10] Samir: one more flag — we should capture a metric for KV cache eviction latency spike (time from eviction decision to first request served post-eviction) because we've seen spike cascades on that.

[00:10:25] Elena: add trace ID propagation so we can stitch fallback traces to customer requests. it's been hard to debug in the past.

[00:10:38] Ravi: agreed. trace tags will be added. I'll also add a debug endpoint to dump local prefix state if we need to triage.

[00:10:50] Priya: small ops ask — can we get a simple diagram that shows the staged degrade path (visual) for sales and customer success to share? non-technical folks asked for it.

[00:11:05] Maya: yep I'll produce a one-pager.

[00:11:10] (long pause, typing)

[00:11:40] Elena: quick question about telemetry retention — for the sims we need high-res traces retained a week longer. is that ok?

[00:11:52] Alex: that's fine for staging, but watch the storage costs. maybe shorter retention but more sampling.

[00:12:05] Samir: or store full traces for a subset of requests (1%) and aggregated for the rest.

[00:12:17] Maya: ok decision: increased retention for full traces for 48 hours, 1% full sample afterwards for a week. aggregate metrics persisted as usual.

[00:12:30] Priya: timeline? when do we want results?

[00:12:35] Maya: target to have initial sim run and kernel fallback doc by next Friday, 2027-07-23. does that sound realistic?

[00:12:45] Alex: yes for docs. sims may complete by Monday 2027-07-26 depending on iteration.

[00:12:55] Ravi: noted. I'll reserve Tuesday night window for runs.

[00:13:05] Maya: ok let's recap action items and owners.

[00:13:15] Priya: recap please Maya.

[00:13:18] Maya: Elena to draft runbook and quality delta notes due 7/22; Alex to create kernel fallback matrix due 7/23; Ravi to run sims and add metrics/traces due 7/26; Samir to script traffic and background tasks due 7/25; Maya to circulate eviction matrix and one-pager by 7/21; Priya to consolidate acceptance criteria and share with stakeholders by 7/21.

[00:13:52] Alex: small thing — mention of competitors: OpenAI and Anthropic have public notes on fallback/perf tradeoffs, and NVIDIA posted an article about kernel optimizations that may apply. i'm putting links in the doc.

[00:14:10] Maya: perfect. any final questions?

[00:14:18] (faint crosstalk)

[00:14:30] Samir: none from me.

[00:14:33] Priya: good.

[00:14:35] Maya: okay thanks everyone. I'll follow up with links and the spreadsheet. meeting adjourned.

[00:14:45] (recording ends)
